Former Nigeria Football Federation President, Amaju Pinnick, says Nigerian football is undergoing a complete restructuring, with plans to remove domestic league clubs from government control. Pinnick said the proposed reforms would extend beyond the football federation to address challenges affecting the domestic league and its clubs. He spoke during an interview on ARISE News published on its website Tuesday, where he identified the domestic league as a critical component of Nigeria’s football development and the future of the sport. “There’s a complete reset when it comes to Nigerian football,” he said. The former NFF president stressed that the restructuring would not focus solely on the federation but would also involve the country’s domestic league. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “It’s not going to be switched to just the Federation. It’s also going to be the league. The league is a major component. “The league is the future. The league is everything. The league will also trickle down to the junior teams among the various clubs,” Pinnick said. He further disclosed that efforts were underway to remove league clubs from government ownership and control as part of the proposed changes. “So, there are a lot of things that I told you that are going on. “Taking the league’s clubs out of government and all that stuff. So, there’s a lot going on, trust me,” he added. Pinnick expressed confidence that the ongoing initiatives would reposition Nigerian football and help restore its standing. The development comes amid renewed calls for structural reforms in Nigerian football, particularly concerning the management of domestic clubs and the development of younger players.
